title: Hubble offers a dazzling necklace
caption: The Necklace Nebula, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Necklace Nebula, PN G054.2-03.4 · constellation Sagitta · about 15000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A glowing ring hangs in space, dotted with dense, bright knots of gas like diamonds on a necklace, with a single bright dot at its centre. This is the Necklace Nebula, a planetary nebula found only recently, made of gas shed by an ordinary star much like the Sun. The ring is about two light-years across.

The central dot is really two stars, only a few million kilometres apart, whirling around each other in little more than a day. About 25 000 years ago one star swelled so much that it swallowed its companion. The smaller star kept orbiting inside the giant, spinning it up until much of its gaseous envelope flew off into space.
Most of that gas escaped along the star's equator, forming the ring. The knots are dense clumps within it, glowing because they absorb ultraviolet light from the central stars.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (1.74 x 1.25 arcminutes) and distance (15000 light years), the frame spans roughly 7.6 × 5.5 light-years. Its light set out about 15,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3 captured the glow of hydrogen (shown in blue), oxygen (green) and nitrogen (red) in visible light.
understand.eye: Filters isolating single gases make each one a separate colour, which is not how an eye would see the blend of light.

behind.people: See full credit: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)
behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: For comparison, Mercury takes 88 days to orbit the Sun, so the central pair's orbit of just over a day is very fast. The nebula lies 15 000 light-years away in Sagitta, the Arrow, and is also catalogued as PN G054.2-03.4.
alt: A glowing ring of gas dotted with bright knots, with a single bright dot in the centre.
